articleTitle: An audio data hiding based on complete complementary codes and its application to an evacuation guiding system
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Information hiding schemes using complete complementary codes (CCCs) have been developed for image data. It has been shown that a high payload and a low bit-error-rate (BER) can be achieved by such data hiding strategies because of the ideal correlation properties of CCCs. In this work, we apply a data hiding scheme based on CCCs to audio signals. Properties such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and BER of the proposed method are investigated through numerical experiments. We also propose to apply the developed data hiding method to an evacuation guiding system. In the proposed system, detailed information on disasters such as earthquakes and tsunamis are embedded into audio signals like sirens. The audio signals in sirens can be processed easily by smartphones and mobile terminals for faster dissemination of disaster information in the community aiding an effective and safe evacucation.

articleTitle: A visible-light communication system using optical CDMA with inverted MPSC
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Visible-light communication systems are suitable to realize secure indoor networks. In this paper, an optical CDMA scheme employing EWO signaling with inverted sequences of MPSC or GMPSC is proposed for visible-light communication systems. The proposed scheme has the property of canceling MUI as well as the conventional EWO-MPSC scheme. Average light intensity and normalized intensity fluctuation of multiplexed optical signals are investigated by computer simulation. It is shown that the proposed scheme is more suitable for visible light communication, since it has lower intensity fluctuation and higher average light intensity, in comparison with the conventional scheme which adopts non-inverted sequences. Then, the authors implemented a visible-light CDM system with several LEDs. It has four channels on each of which 31.25KHz MIDI data, coded with a generalized MPSC with a length of 64, is transmitted. It is confirmed that the system can correctly decode every MIDI data transmitted simultaneously.

articleTitle: New optimum frequency hopping sequences derived from fermat quotients
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Two classes of optimum frequency hopping sequences (FHSs) derived from Fermat quotient with respect to the Lempel-Greenberger bound are presented. The constructed p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-periodic sequences are defined over ℤ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> and have the maximum Hamming autocorrelation p, where p is a prime. Also, we give a new optimum family of sequences with size p. Moreover, we interpret the constructed sequences in terms of new partition sets of ℤ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p2</sub>*, which is very useful for implementation considerations.

articleTitle: Joint ABS power and resource allocations for eICIC in heterogeneous networks
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Heterogeneous networks (HetNets) are expected to be one of the major performance enhancement enablers of LTE-Advanced. In order to protect pico-UEs from the strong macro interference, the macro eNBs need to reduce the transmission power during protected subframes instead of suspending data transmission introduced in 3GPP Release 10, scheduling strictly users in the vicinity of the macro eNBs. In this paper, based on low power (LP) almost blank subframes (ABS), we study a joint optimization of power allocation of ABS (called dynamic LP-ABS) and resource allocation to maximize the total throughput. The proposed algorithm takes into account the power allocation of ABSs in the marco eNB, the ABS partition and the UE association in all cells. Simulation results show that dynamic LP-ABS can effectively increase system throughput compared to the fixed LP-ABS and zero-ABS.

articleTitle: A binarization of geometric sequences with Legendre symbol and its autocorrelation
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Let p be an odd characteristic and m be the degree of primitive polynomial f(x). Let ω be its zero, that is a primitive element in F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pm</sub>*, then the sequence S = {s<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>}, s<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> = Tr (ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>) for i = 0, 1, 2, ... becomes a maximum length sequence, where Tr (·) is the trace function over F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>. On this fact, this paper proposes to binarize the sequence by using Legendre symbol. It will be a class of geometric sequences but its properties such as the period and autocorrelation has not been discussed. Then, it is shown that the obtained binary sequence (geometric sequence with Legendre symbol) has the period L given by 2(p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> - 1)/(p-1) and a certain periodic autocorrelation. After that, this paper also shows the numbers of ones and minus ones in the proposed binary sequence per a period together with some small examples.

articleTitle: Randomness properties of stream ciphers for wireless communications
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper we evaluate the randomness properties of four synchronous stream ciphers for use in wireless communications. These ciphers are: SNOW 3G, ZUC, and AES, all of which are a part of the current LTE standard, and the WG-16 stream cipher. The randomness testing is performed with the NIST SP 800-22 test suite, and its results are accordingly tabulated. In addition, we also examine the autocorrelation properties of the keystreams.

articleTitle: A physical layer secure wireless communication scheme for high speed railway
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: The high speed railway wireless communication system is much different from public wireless communication system, because the service is train control messages, which is closely related to the safety of train transportation. Thus it is much demanding to the security and reliability. To guarantee the train control messages delivery security, secrecy capacity and outage probability at the high speed railway scenario under single-stream beamforming are analyzed and show that the security requirements can not been satisfied. Thus a physical layer secure wireless communications scheme under beamforming with artificial noise is proposed for high speed railway. In this scheme, artificial noise is used in the null space of the main channel only to degrade the eavesdropper's channel. Simulation results illustrate the proposed scheme decreases the outage probability under a certain secrecy capacity demand, and meets the secure communication requirements.

articleTitle: Non-linear fast fading compensation for HTRCI-MIMO/OFDM with QRM-MLD and channel ranking
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO/OFDM) systems, large complexity is considerable work. To mitigate this problem, high time resolution carrier interferometry (HTRCI) for MIMO/OFDM applying QR decomposition with M algorithm maximum likelihood detection (QRM-MLD) and channel ranking has been proposed. In the fast fading environment, since many errors are occurred in the last part of the packet, the decision direct method has been proposed. However, it requires also large complexity. Therefore, in this paper, we propose the non-linear prediction method for a HTRCI-MIMO/OFDM with QRM-MLD and channel ranking.

articleTitle: Low-peak factor optimal zero-correlation zone sequence set and its applications
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: The present paper introduces a novel method for the construction of sequences that have a zero-correlation zone. For the proposed sequence set, both the cross-correlation function and the side lobe of the auto-correlation function are zero for phase shifts within the zero-correlation zone. The proposed sequence set can be generated from an arbitrary Hadamard matrix of order n and a set of 2n trigonometric-like function sequences of length 4n. The proposed construction can generate an optimal sequence set that satisfies, for a given zero-correlation zone and sequence period, the theoretical bound on the number of members. The peak factor of the proposed sequence set is equal to √2.

articleTitle: A study on the Lyapunov exponents of sequences generated by the logistic map over integers
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: We are interested in the properties of sequences generated by the logistic map over integers. In the present paper, we give the Lyapunov exponents of the sequences generated by the map. Then, we confirm good correlations between a sign of the exponents and a few properties of randomness such as averages periods and link-lengths, and an occurrence rate of `0' bit in the generated sequence. Then, we prove that the exponent indicates stability of the sequence.

articleTitle: Long huffman sequences derived from even functional quadratic residues
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Huffman sequences with long length are generated for the application to high attenuation sonar or radar. A general expression of Huffman sequence is given by polynomial expansion of its spectrum. For long length, the fist-order approximate sequence is given by a DFT expression and the estimate absolute value of the sequence is represented by a Gaussian shape. Long Huffman sequences are constructed from even functional quadratic residues. The calculated sequences with length up to 15914 show their estimate absolute values of Gaussian shape with peak value 2, although the maximum absolute value is about 6 when the length is 6030. The maximum absolute values are expected to be decreased by parameter selections.

articleTitle: A study on distance between two sequences by the logistic map over integers with slightly different parameters
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: One of our investigation purposes is to give a design guide of a pseudorandom number generator using the logistic map with finite precision. In the present paper, we show that two sequences for slightly different parameters are completely different from each other, even if the logistic map has the same computational precision and the same initial values. First, we decide the arithmetic precision and the initial value. Second, we obtain two sequences by the logistic map for slightly different parameters. Last, we estimate a correlation of them by measuring the distance between two elements.

articleTitle: Frequency hopping sequences with optimal partial Hamming correlation by interleaving techniques
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In order to evaluate the goodness of frequency hopping (FH) sequence design, the periodic Hamming correlation function is used as an important measure. Usually, the length of correlation window is shorter than the period of the chosen FH sequence, so the study of the partial Hamming correlation of FH sequence is particularly important. In this paper, we first prove that there does not exist a strictly optimal FH sequence set of family size M and length N over a frequency slot set of size q with respect to the partial Hamming correlation bound when N > q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> over M and q ≥ 2. In addition, we give a construction of FH sequences with optimal partial Hamming correlation by utilizing interleaving techniques.

articleTitle: On relationship between proposed lower bound and well-known bounds for cyclic codes
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: There have been useful lower bounds for the minimum distance of a cyclic code, BCH bound, Hartmann-Tzeng bound, Roos bound and Shift bound. The authors proposed a lower bound of minimum distance by discrete Fourier transform (DFT) in 2010. The relationship between BCH bound, Hartmann-Tzeng bound and Roos bound, BCH bound, Hartmann-Tzeng bound and Shift bound are known, respectively. However, it's unknown the relationship between Roos bound, Shift bound and Proposed bound. In this paper, we discuss this relation with the cyclic codes.

articleTitle: IQ imbalance estimation and compensation schemes based on time frequency interferometry for OFDM
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: A direct-conversion receiver (DCR) reduces the power consumption and cost. However, DCR in Orthogonal frequency division multiplex (OFDM) systems suffer from IQ imbalance. Until this time, many algorithms are proposed to compensate IQ imbalance in OFDM. However, the complexity is still considerable work. On the other hand, time-frequency interferometry-OFDM (TFI-OFDM) system has been proposed to achieve an accurate channel identification property with small number of pilot symbols. In this paper, we propose a novel IQ imbalance estimation and compensation scheme using TFI-OFDM system. In the proposed system, by using the feature of the TFI pilot symbols, we can identify IQ imbalance without high calculation complexity. Furthermore, by using subcarrier selection, the influence of the noise power can be reduced. From the simulation results, the proposed scheme can achieve the low-complexity IQ imbalance estimation and compensation without a degradation of the BER performance.

articleTitle: 64-QAM complementary sets for high-rate OFDM transmissions
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Existing 64-QAM Golay complementary pairs, each having impulse-like aperiodic auto-correlation sums, have been used to generate codebooks in code-keying orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) communications for the peak-to-mean power control. As a generalization of the 64-QAM Golay complementary pairs, in this paper, 64-QAM complementary sets, each of which contains two or more sequences, are proposed. It is shown that when the set size is not less than 4, they lead to significant code rate increases in code-keying OFDM communications.

articleTitle: On correlation properties of 4-phase with zero points from constant-weight sequences over GF(5)
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: We proposed a method for constructing constant-weight and multi-valued sequences from the cyclic difference sets by generalization of the method in binary case proposed by N.Li, X.Zeng and L.Hu in 2008. In this paper we give some properties about a set of such sequences by constant-weight sequences over GF(5) with length 21 from the (21, 5, 1)-cyclic difference set. It has almost highest linear complexities and good profiles of all sequences' linear complexities. Moreover we investigate new correlations method as the 4-phase with zero points for a set of sequences over GF(5) with length 21 and an example is given.

articleTitle: On fast synchronization acquisition of ZCZ-CDMA
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: ZCZ-CDMA operating under quasi-synchronous timing control and using zero correlation zone (ZCZ) code possesses interference free performance and fast frame acquisition. This paper discusses fast synchronization acquisition methods using a matched filter bank, which simultaneously calculates correlation between a received signal and any sequence in ZCZ code, and the effectiveness is shown from synchronization error rates (SER) on the AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels.

articleTitle: Sequences, randomness and security
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: The definition of of randomness and pseudorandomness in the context of sequence generation is far from controversial. We provide a survey of some approaches to randomness, including: 1. Information theoretic (i.e., probabilistic) approaches, such as those based on Shannon and Renyi entropies, and 2. Complexity theoretic approaches based essentially on Kolmogorov complexity. We discuss the settings where one approach may be superior to the other. We also consider the design and analysis of randomness tests, illustrating it with some examples.

articleTitle: Optimal frequency hopping sequence sets from MDS codes
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we present a class of punctured codes from maximum distance separable (MDS) codes given by Ezerman, Grassl, and Solé in 2011. Choosing the left shift distinct sequences from every full-cycle equivalence class, we obtain a class of FH sequence sets, the parameters of which meet the Singleton bound on the maximum Hamming correlation of FH sequences.

articleTitle: Design of PN codes for optical wireless code-shift-keying with IM/DD
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: A pseudo-noise (PN) code used by code shift keying (CSK) for optical wireless communication with intensity-modulation and direct detection (IM/DD) are considered. Since CSK has the several PN codes, the data transmission rate and the bit error rate (BER) performance can improve by increasing the number of PN codes. However, the conventional optical PN codes are not suitable for optical CSK with IM/DD because the ratio of the number of PN codes and the code length of PN code, M/L is smaller than 1/√L. In this paper, a new PN code, which combines the generalized modified prime sequence code (GMPSC) with Hadamard code is proposed. The proposed PN code can achieve M/L = 1. Moreover, the symbol error rate performance is analyzed under the additive white Gaussian noise channel. It is found that CSK with the proposed PN code outperforms the conventional optical CSK system.

articleTitle: Capacity enhancement using cooperative distributed antenna system under LOS MIMO channels in high speed train scenario
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: This paper presents a capacity enhancement algorithm by using cooperative transmission in distributed antenna system (DAS) under line-of-sight (LOS) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) channels in high speed train scenario. In this algorithm, the Base Band Unit (BBU) of the DAS selects multiple Remote Antenna Units (RAU) according to the large-scale fading parameters, and cooperative transmission is then performed among these RAUs to increase channel capacity. WINNER II channel model is considered for the capacity analysis. Simulation results show that cooperative transmission greatly increases capacity under LOS MIMO channels in high speed train scenario.

articleTitle: Method for extending parallel combinatory multi-code transmission with constant-amplitude signaling
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In multi-code transmission system, the amplitude of the transmission signal may have sharp fluctuations, and non-linear distortion occurs in the transmission signal. To solve this problem, the authors propose two novel multi-code transmission systems with constant amplitude signaling in this paper. They compare the proposed systems with Multi-Code transmission with Constant Amplitude signaling (MC-CA) system and Parallel Combinatory Multi-Code transmission with Constant Amplitude signaling (PCMC-CA) system, from the point of view of the bit error rate (BER) performance and the amount of transmitted data. As a result, they showed that the BER performance of the proposed systems are better than that of MC-CA system in the high E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> domain. They also showed that the amount of transmitted data of one of the proposed systems is 1.125 times as much as that of MC-CA system.

articleTitle: Optical wireless LDPC-coded PPM with unequal transmission power allocation scheme
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, the low density parity check (LDPC) coded schemes with unequal transmission power allocation (UTPA) in optical wireless channel is evaluated. In particular, the bit error rate performance of the LDPC coded binary pulse position with UTPA is investigated in the presence of APD noise, thermal noise, scintillation. Consequently, the BER performance of the LDPC coded pulse position modulation with UTPA is better than that of the conventional LDPC coded pulse position modulation. It is found that there is optimum power ratio (R) and optimum R is varied by each average received laser power per slot (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sub>). For example, when variance of scintillation is 0.1, the optimum R is 4.0 at P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sub> =-50[dBm]. Thus, the LDPC coded pulse position modulation with UTPA system is superior to the conventional system with R=1.0.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of BER performance of spread spectrum system using a huffman sequence over rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we theoretically analyse the influence by intersymbol interference (ISI) on the bit error rate (BER) performance of the spread spectrum (SS) system using a real-valued Huffman sequence whose aperiodic correlation function has zero sidelobes except at the left and right shift-ends, under the quasi-static Rayleigh fading environment. The system can give the unified communication and ranging system because the output of a matched filter (MF) is the ideal impulse by overlap of 1 chip. As a result, the BER performance of the system under the quasi-static Rayleigh fading environment is improved with decrease in the absolute value of the shift-end value, is not influenced by ISI if the shift-end value is almost zero-value.

articleTitle: Channel parameter extraction methodology for system-level simulator in small cell environments
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Small cell networks have many attractive solutions to solve the network overload caused by heavy demands of traffic. To evaluate the performance of systems, a system-level simulator (SLS) is typically used. However, the performance evaluation with a typical channel parameter set which is representing the entire area in SLS shows only the typical performance of the entire area, so that extra field trial is necessary to evaluate realistic deployment performance of a given region. In this paper, a channel parameter extraction methodology is proposed by using a ray tracing tool to evaluate a realistic performance of a target region for SLS.

articleTitle: Joint time and frequency domain double differential detection and equalization for DFT scrambling vector OFDM under fast fading channels
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Although differential detection and equalization with scrambling decision feedback can help DFT scrambling vector OFDM (DFT-SV-OFDM) system under frequency-selective fading channels with channel estimation errors, however, high mobility which caused random Doppler frequency shift may significantly degrade the achievable BER performance. In this paper, a new joint time and frequency domain double differential detection and equalization is proposed for DFT-SV-OFDM system, where differential detection is fulfilled both in time and frequency. Compared with the two existing systems, the new scheme shows more robust under the rapidly time-varying fading channels.

articleTitle: Distributed Frequency Synchronization for OFDMA-based wireless mesh networks
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the synchronization for OFDMA-based wireless mesh networks and analyze the effect of carrier frequency misalignment between distributed nodes. Based on our previous work, so called, Distributed Frequency Synchronization (DFS), we propose a modified DFS (mDFS). The proposed scheme incorporates some practical issues, not considered in the previous DFS scheme. Simulation results show that mDFS works also well, and confirm that both mDFS and DFS are efficient and useful.

articleTitle: Difference sets, sequences, and multipliers
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: It is well known that sequences with good autocorrelation properties are closely related to cyclic difference sets. In my talk, I will survey some not well known types of difference sets related to sequences. I will also summarize some multiplier theorems for difference sets and discuss their implication for sequences.

articleTitle: Experiments of long distance wireless communication on spread spectrum
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: A spread spectrum technology is known to be able to expand the distance of wireless communications by improving the processing gain. However, the effective processing gain is decreased due to the phase shift between the two transceivers. We have studied the compensation algorithm of this phase shift, and its performance has been evaluated by a computer simulation. This paper shows some experimental results of wireless communication using spread spectrum with this algorithm on handheld transceivers.

articleTitle: An enhanced frequency-shifted reference ultrawideband scheme for low data rate applications
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: A frequency shifted reference ultrawideband (FSR-UWB) scheme has been proposed for low data rate applications to reduce the receiver complexity of the traditional transmitted-reference UWB (TR-UWB) scheme. However, the FSR-UWB is rather energy inefficient since one bit information is delivered by two pulses in a frame. In this paper, we propose an enhanced FSR-UWB scheme which can send the multiple bits in the two orthogonal pulses shifted by different frequencies in a frame. The results from analysis and simulation show that the proposed scheme provides an SNR gain of 1.5 dB over the conventional FSR scheme at the same data rate.

articleTitle: Strong tracking filter modeling for GPS robust navigation
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Efficient implementation of positioning algorithm plays a crucial role in modern Global Positioning System (GPS). Conventional non-linear Least Squares (LS) method is applied iteratively by Taylor expansion, which doesn't combine different epoch-time for mutual restraint. While with respect to generally used extended Kalman filter (EKF), it requires an accurate system model estimation and exact stochastic Gaussian white noise, resulting in non-uniformly convergence with an unknown bias or model error. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a Strong Tracking Filter (STF) modeling. To achieve robustness about model uncertainty and tracking capability on the mutation status, the STF adjusts the real-time state prediction error covariance matrix and the corresponding gain matrix. It also makes use of Time-varying Fading Factor (TVFF) to deal with the past data, which weakens the stale data to the impact of current filtered value. Simulation shows that the proposed STF is capable of enhancing more than half precision than traditional EKF and LS.

articleTitle: On the modified pseudo-ternary M-sequence pair
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we described the properties of the modified pseudo-ternary M-sequence (MPTM) pair, which consists of the MPTM and {-1, 1}-valued M-sequence, such as the generating MPTM pair, the orthogonality, the expansion of MPTM, the cross-correlation, and the S-curve characteristic. MPTM is a PN code which combines the {0, 1}-valued M-sequence with the Hadamard code. The S-curve characteristic is the same as that of the conventional direct sequence spread-spectrum (DS/SS) system using M-sequence. Thus, the tracking system with MPTM pair can use that of DS/SS system.

articleTitle: On the optimized complex field network coding design in cooperative relay transmission
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Wireless relay and network coding are two critical techniques to improve the reliability and increase the throughput for wireless cooperative communications. In this paper, the performance analysis is presented at first to highlight the optimized coding coefficient and power design in wireless relay cooperative transmission system with complex field network coding (CFNC) plus relay selection. It is validated that, the reasonable choices of the coding coefficients as well as the optimal power allocation can significantly improve the wireless relay cooperative transmission.

articleTitle: Properties and crosscorrelation of decimated Sidelnikov sequences
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we show that the d-decimation of a Sidelnikov sequence is the d-multiple of another Sidelnikov sequence and vice versa. Also, we calculate the crosscorrelation magnitude between d- and d′-decimations of a Sidelnikov sequence of period q − 1 to be upper bounded by (d+d′ − 1) √q+3.

articleTitle: Linear channel estimation and training for frequency-selective fading channels in two-way relay networks
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: The linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) estimation of frequency selective fading channels is addressed in two-way relay networks. We estimate the channel responses required for self-interference cancelation and coherent detection in the time domain. The optimal training condition for the minimization of the mean square error (MSE) of the LMMSE estimator is derived and, taking into account the peak-to-average power ratio, new training sequences satisfying the optimal training condition are proposed. It is shown that the LMMSE estimator significantly outperforms the least square (LS) estimator in the low SNR regime and that the LMMSE estimator is less sensitive to the training sequences than the LS estimator.

articleTitle: Optimal two-dimensional variable-weight optical orthogonal codes via scarce mixed difference families
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: A 2-D variable-weight OOC (2-D VWOOC) is a set of 0, 1 matrices with variable weight, good auto and cross-correlations, it was first introduced to meet multiple QoS (Quality of Service) requirements in fiber optic communications. In this paper, two new infinite classes of optimal 2-D VWOOCs are constructed.

articleTitle: Multicarrier transmission systems with spreading sequences in large delay spread channel
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In multi-carrier transmission systems, MC-CDMA and MC-DS-CDMA have been proposed. However, when large delay spread is longer than guard interval (GI), the inter symbol interference (ISI) and inter carrier interference (ICI) are occurred. Their interferences cause the system performance deterioration. This paper treats MC-CDMA and MC-DS-CDMA with four kinds of orthogonal spreading sequence including even-shift orthogonal sequences (E-sequence) type zero correlation zone (E-ZCZ) code in large delay spread channel. Moreover, interleaving method is considered in MC-DS-CDMA. Finally, the bit error rate (BER) performance is evaluated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Distributed interference channel based resource allocation for network-assisted device-to-device communications
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced distributed resource allocation scheme for device-to-device (D2D) communication using loose network-assistance, namely distributed interference channel based resource allocation (DICRA). The MAC/PHY protocol of the proposed DICRA is described and the performance advantage over FlashLinQ is confirmed from computer simulation results.

articleTitle: On the correlation properties of generalized chirp-like sequences and their application
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: A generalized chirp-like (GCL) sequence is constructed by modulating a Zadoff-Chu sequence with a unimodular sequence. Under some specific conditions, the magnitude of the cross-correlation between GCL sequences is known to be the same as that of the corresponding Zadoff-Chu sequences. In this paper, we further investigate the conditions under which such a relation holds. Using them, we construct a new class of optimal zero-correlation zone (ZCZ) sequences.

articleTitle: Degraded multiple-access channel with confidential messages
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we study the degraded multiple-access channel (MAC) with confidential messages, where two users transmit their confidential messages (no common message) to a destination, and each user obtains a degraded version of the output of the MAC. Each user views the other user as a eavesdropper, and wishes to keep its confidential message as secret as possible from the other user. Measuring each users uncertainty about the other users confidential message by equivocation, the inner and outer bounds on the capacity equivocation region for this model have been provided. The result is further explained via the binary and Gaussian examples.

articleTitle: An efficient carrier frequency offset estimate for MIMO-OFDM in LTE system
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: The problem of pilot assisted carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation in LTE system is investigated in this paper. Since both the pilot design and the number of pilot symbols are already fixed in LTE technical standards, it is proposed to employ multiple successive pilot symbols to improve the CFO estimation performance under the LTE standard constraints. We firstly present the generalized CRLB (GCRLB) analysis based on multiple successive pilot symbols. It is revealed that, better CFO estimate can be achieved by jointly using multiple successive pilot symbols than by using only one pilot symbol. The enhanced maximum likelihood (ML) carrier frequency offset estimate problem is formulated and simulation results are presented to validate that the proposed CFO estimate scheme offers an effective mechanism to improve the CFO estimate in practical LTE system.

articleTitle: Integer-forcing receiver for MC-CDMA system
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Integer-forcing (IF) linear receiver has been recently introduced for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) fading channels. The integer coefficients have to be chosen based on the channel realizations, and the choice of such coefficients is known to determine the receiver performance. It has been proved that Integer-forcing receiver outperforms the minimum mean square estimator (MMSE) and zero-forcing (ZF) linear receivers in MIMO. In this paper, we propose Integer-forcing receiver for Multi-Carrier Code Division Multiple Access (MC-CDMA) systems. The Integer-forcing receiving algorithm for MC-CDMA is derived. The simulation results show that the bit error rate (BER) of Integer-forcing algorithm can approach the Maximum-likelihood (ML) performance with a few decibels, and largely outperforms other linear receivers, such as MMSE and ZF.

articleTitle: On large zero auto/cross correlation zone of Golay/QAM Golay sequences and their applications and related correlation properties
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Golay sequences have been studied for more than five decades since Golay first discovered those sequences, which have found many applications in communications, especially, for peak average power ratio reduction in orthogonal frequency division multiple (OFDM) systems in recent cellular communication. However, the periodic auto- correlation of a single Golay sequence is unknown. In this talk, I will present our recent results on zero correlation zones of Golay sequences. First we show that there exists three different classes of Golay sequences with a zero auto- correlation zone (ZACZ) of length approximately an half, a quarter or one eighth of their period. Those zones can also be hold for zero crosscorrelation zone (ZCCZ). Furthermore, the large ZACZ or ZCCZ of Golay sequences can be inherited by QAM Golay sequences. Those new findings on Golay sequences can be explored during synchronization and detection at the receiver end and thus improve the performance of the communication system. As an example, we present the application of binary Golay sequences with ZACZ for intersymbol interference (ISI) channel estimation and show the comparisons of the performance of Golay- sequence-aided channel estimation with m-sequences and Frank-Zadoff-Chu sequences. Finally, we consider different measurements for correlation of sequences. We show that three classes of Golay/QAM Golay sequences have the same large zero correlation zones as above when it is measured by odd correlation. The content of the talk is taken from the series of joint work with Fei Hou and Yang Yang.

articleTitle: Reliable transmission schemes for train control information in high-speed railway
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: The reliability of wireless communication systems in high-speed railway, especially the reliable transmission of train control information, has attracted a lot of attention. With the decision of global system for mobile communication for railway (GSM-R) evolution to long-term evolution (LTE) for railway by International Union of Railways (ITU), many techniques such as redundant transmission and low order modulation and coding scheme (MCS) without adaption like PDCCH are considered to enhance the reliability of train control information. In the paper, two PHY-diversity reliable transmission schemes adapted to train location are proposed. Then, the closed form expression for SER (Symbol Error Rate) of these schemes experiencing the Ricean-faded channel is derived. The numerical results show that, in the scenario whose SNR is larger than 10dB, the proposed schemes can dramatically decrease the transmission SER.

articleTitle: Potential of improper-complex signaling in communications over two-user interference channel
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we show a potential of improper-complex signaling in multi-user proper-complex Gaussian noise channel. It is well known that improper-signaling does not increase the capacity of a single-user and some multi-user proper-complex Gaussian noise channels. As a baseline system, we apply the conventional iterative water filling (IWF) algorithm to two-user interference channel, where each user transmits proper-complex signal in order to maximize its own information rate. To demonstrate the potential of improper-complex signaling, we consider a special two-user interference channel, where each transmitter has single transmit antenna, each receiver also has single receive antenna, equal-gain direct links and general asymmetric-gain cross links. By using exhaustive search, we find the capacity region of this communication system and compares it with that obtained by the conventional IWF. It turns out that, depending on the magnitudes of the cross channel gains, the improper-complex signaling outperforms the selfish IWF algorithm that generates proper-complex signals. This warrants further research on the application of the improper-complex signaling to various channel models with constraints on the level of user cooperation.

articleTitle: Some properties of 2-dimensional array structure of Sidelnikov sequences of period qd − 1
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we show that the generalization by D.S.Kim in 2010 for the construction of sequence family of period q−1 using the Sidelnikov sequences of period q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>−1 can be further generalized by removing the condition that gcd(q − 1, d) = 1. It turned out that the correlation bound remains the same and the size of the family is almost the same as the one with the previous condition.

articleTitle: Trial of free-space parallel transmission system based on optical ZCZ-CDMA system
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: In this paper, we manufacture the parallel transmission system consisting of an infrared light emitting diode (LED), an avalanche photo diode (APD) module and a field programmable gate array (FPGA) board corresponding to 132, 540 logic elements (LEs) by way of trial, and evaluate the BER performance of the optical ZCZ-CDMA system with the equal gain combining (EGC) by the indoor experiment. As a result of indoor experiment with the parallel transmission system, BER performance improves with an increase in number of received APD by the EGC.

articleTitle: Preface
publicationTitle: The Sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications
abstract: Welcome to the sixth International Workshop on Signal Design and Its Applications in Communications (IWSDA'13) held in Tokyo, Japan, between October 27 to November 1, 2013. The first IWSDA was held in September 2001 in Chengdu, China, the second in Yamaguchi, Japan in October 2005, the third in Chengdu again in September 2007, the fourth in Fukuoka, Japan in October 2009, and the fifth in Guilin, China in October 2011. It is well-known that discrete signal design plays a very important role in widespread applications, such as spread spectrum, code division multiple access, positioning, channel estimations, synchronization, optimal detections, etc. The aim of this workshop is to foster fruitful interactions among signal designers, coding theorists, cryptographic researchers and communications practitioners from all over the world. This volume contains the refereed proceedings of the IWSDA'13.
